title: Framework isomers controlled by the speed of cryst
one_line_summary: Design rule: control crystallization speed during synthesis of Zn(L)(bdc)0.5 framework isomers

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] control crystallization speed during synthesis of Zn(L)(bdc)0.5 framework isomers → enables formation of different framework isomers and structural diversity, including distinct 4·82 and 4·6·12 nets

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [neutral] use quicker crystallization speed → shifts the obtained layer topology from 4·82 to 4·6·12

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: polymer 1 vs polymer 2: winner=tie on layer_topology

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: polymer 1 synthesized with gradual program-controlled cooling vs polymer 2 synthesized with ambient cooling: winner=tie on crystallization_condition

key_insights.title: Failure
key_insights.body: [performance_regression] use framework isomers 1 and 2 for N2 and CO2 adsorption despite their very small apertures: no obvious N2 and CO2 adsorption was observed

notable_quotes: Two framework isomers, Zn(L)(bdc)0.5·0.25H2O (1) and Zn(L)(bdc)0.5·0.17H2O (2), were obtained solely by controlling crystallization speed.
Although 1 and 2 have similar Zn coordination and ligand binding, slight tetrahedral-angle differences generate distinct 2D layers and 3D nets.
These self-penetrating (3,4)-connected nets differ from known boracite-, Pt3O4-, jph-, C3N4-, and tfz-type nets by showing only two-fold catenation.
